scores.notes: The stone leaves most of the circular pit mouth wide open while the king presses a seal onto the slab and a lord presses a separate seal onto the opposite rim across the open gap. In the upper left, three laborers also pull a rope tied to a pickaxe stuck into empty dirt.

Shows Rephaiah and builders hoisting and setting stones onto the damaged wall of Jerusalem with the temple mount behind them. Tools, ropes, poses, and anatomy are coherent with no lettering or edge issues.
A prominent bearded prophet with a staff stands on the left preaching to a crowd of weary listeners, inserting the speaker/narrator into his own poetic verse when the text does not call for him.

Playing-card corner index letters ('A' and inverted 'A'/'C' on the center card soldier, and a 'J'-like index on the lower-left card soldier) are clearly visible, though they are unreadable corner indices rather than words. Otherwise the courtroom scene, tall Alice in a yellow dress, spectacled White Rabbit, and animal jury match the text and rules.

The king presses his signet into wax over a cord binding the stone laid across the den's mouth while lords wait on the right holding their own signets and laborers stand left with levers and rope. Clean ink-and-watercolor execution with no lettering or anatomical flaws.

Faint horizontal rows of unreadable pseudo-script squiggles are drawn across the unrolled scroll held by the priests in the center. The rest of the temple-courtyard scene with Hezekiah directing the work and law is coherent and well drawn.

The Caterpillar is given an explicitly human face (nose, lips, eyelids, double chin) plus a bowler hat and waistcoat, breaking the rule that talking animals have animal faces and only text-given dress. Scale is also contradictory: Alice stands next to a shoulder-high giant mushroom, yet a miniature cottage on the far right is only knee-high to her.

A dense cloud rests directly over the Tabernacle in the middle of the Israelite tent encampment while families and shepherds remain settled in camp in the foreground. No lettering, human shape in the cloud, or anatomical defects.

In the right foreground, a stonemason holds two hammers simultaneously—one raised in his right hand and a second hammer held horizontally in his left where a chisel should be—while the worker behind him raises an empty fist aimlessly.

Background players carry wooden croquet mallets and metal wire croquet hoops are planted right beside the doubled-up card soldiers, contradicting the live-flamingo mallets and soldier arches. The crowned King on the right is also drawn as a flat playing card with stick limbs instead of a person in court-card dress.

Unreadable pale pseudo-script lettering is painted across the side panel of the rightmost fire-engine wagon in front of the burning whitewashed house. Otherwise the group hastening down the hill road toward the blazing house and three fire engines matches the passage cleanly.

Depicts Holmes, Watson, the bandaged engineer pointing, the station-master with lantern, and police arriving along the hill road before the blazing whitewashed house and three horse-drawn fire engines spraying water. No lettering, screen likenesses, or anatomical flaws.

Shows the towering pillar of cloud remaining over the Tabernacle surrounded by the vast Israelite camp, with foreground figures tending fires, flocks, and conversing while encamped. Cleanly composed with no faults.

Captures Alice grown tall in a yellow dress arguing with the King and Queen in court-card dress while the spectacled White Rabbit holds the blank scroll of verses and animal jurors sit with blank slates. Soldiers are flat cards with suit pips only, with no lettering or depiction-rule violations.

Depicts townspeople filling storehouses, jars, sacks, and treasure chests with grain, oil, fabrics, and silver beneath radiant sunbeams, with no personified figure of Wisdom. Anatomy, setting, and composition are clean and free of lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor view of the massive cloud resting over the Tabernacle amid rows of Israelite tents, with foreground campers conversing and cooking. No lettering, unpainted edges, or anatomical flaws.

Unreadable vertical squiggles/pseudo-writing appear on the folded paper Holmes holds in the center and on a sheet sticking out from the stack on the table. Otherwise the Baker Street scene of Lestrade leaning over to point at the opposite side of the bill from Holmes is spot-on.

Unreadable horizontal lines of pseudo-script appear on the printed slip Watson holds to the window light, on the letters spread beneath Holmes's left hand on the lower-right table, and on the folded newspaper beside them. The composition, expressions, and Victorian styling otherwise match the passage well.

Shows Rephaiah standing on scaffolding helping set a stone block into Jerusalem's wall while builders lever the stone, hoist, and mix mortar with the walled city behind. Coherent tools, poses, and anatomy with no lettering.

Shows an apostle/teacher lecturing a seated audience from an unrolled scroll covered in unreadable rows of pseudo-script squiggles, inserting the speaker and listeners into a poetic epistle verse. Meanwhile the bronze mirror sits unused on a side table with nobody looking dimly into it.

Depicts open storehouses and townspeople carrying sacks of grain, amphorae, loaves, and baskets of woven goods in a prosperous walled town, without personifying Wisdom. Figures, poses, and setting are coherent and free of lettering.

Beneath the Dormouse's armchair under the tablecloth, two oversized grey furry legs stand on the grass while a separate tiny pink splayed paw also pokes up onto the tablecloth right in front of the Dormouse, giving it impossible extra limbs.

Dark horizontal squiggle lines of unreadable pseudo-script are drawn on the white page under the seated scribe's pen at the table in the lower left. The rest of the temple courtyard scene with Hezekiah, the priest, and offerings is clean and well rendered.

The watercolor wash fades to unpainted white paper along the top-left, top-right, and bottom-right corners, which this item accepts. The priest casting feathers and the bird's crop onto the ash heap beside the horned bronze altar matches Leviticus 1:16 accurately and without gore.

The priest holds an intact, headed dove over the ash pile rather than casting away only the removed crop and feathers (contradicting the prior verse where its head was already wrung off and burned). In addition, the white courtyard curtain fence cuts right across the front entrance of the Tabernacle tent.

The stone lid leaves a wide crescent opening along the entire front of the den while the king presses his palm flat into clay with his signet ring facing upward on his knuckle and another puddle of sealing clay sitting under his sandal. On the right, a worker also holds a loop of rope attached to nothing.

The small white price-tag card tucked into the Mad Hatter's hatband on the right displays tiny unreadable dark numeral/glyph marks. Otherwise the outdoor tea-party scene with indignant Alice in a yellow dress, the March Hare, sleeping Dormouse, and tea-only table matches the text closely.

Prominent rows of unreadable pseudo-script squiggles cover the printed slip Watson holds up to the window, the papers stacked across the foreground desk, and the sheets on Holmes's lap (plus dial marks on the mantel clock). The characters, setting, and action otherwise fit the passage.

A prominent bearded prophet with a staff stands on a rocky ledge on the right gesturing upward/outward while a listener sits at his feet in the lower-right corner, inserting the speaker/narrator into his own poetic declaration.

Faithfully illustrates indignant Alice in an armchair at the end of the long outdoor tea table under the tree, with the March Hare resting his arm on the sleeping Dormouse beside the Hatter (whose hat has no card or lettering) and only tea on the table. Anatomy, dress, and details are clean throughout.

Depicts Rephaiah in an embroidered blue tunic setting a large stone block onto Jerusalem's broken wall while masons mortar, carry stone baskets, and hoist blocks on ropes. Coherent composition, anatomy, and setting with no lettering.

Shows the tearful Mock Turtle singing and the Gryphon waving its clawed forepaws as both dance solemnly beside Alice (in a yellow dress) on the shingle shore without lobsters. Clean anatomy, accurate hybrid creatures, and no lettering or unpainted edges.
